<!-- SOURCE: ai/agent-instructions.md -->

---
title: MXNI instructions for AI agents
---

# MXNI instructions for AI agents

This document is the compact behavioral contract for AI systems generating MXNI interfaces, graphics, or implementation code.

## Brand

MXNI is a balanced futuristic technology identity: technical, modular, expressive, and legible.

## Visual constraints

- Default dark background: `#09070D`.
- Surface: `#15111C`.
- Elevated surface: `#211A2B`.
- Primary brand: `#A83FE0`.
- Secondary accent: `#E044C5`.
- Technical/interaction accent: `#24CDE0`.
- Limited highlight: `#B5F52D`.
- Display font: Manrope.
- Technical font: JetBrains Mono.
- Radius scale: 2, 6, 10 px.
- Spacing scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 px.

## Composition

Prefer modular grids, controlled rectangular geometry, clear hierarchy, and negative space. Use subtle technical textures and localized glow. Avoid generic cyberpunk, excessive neon, random circuit patterns, rainbow gradients, and decorative noise.

## Product adaptation

Keep foundations consistent. Adapt density, navigation, semantic colors, and composition to the product's task. Do not force a marketing layout into a functional application.

## Accessibility

Target WCAG 2.2 AA. Use semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, visible focus, reduced motion, accessible labels, and non-color status cues.

## Platforms

Identify the target platform before designing or coding and follow its guide:

- Web (browser sites and web apps): `platforms/web/` or `/llms-web.txt`.
- Desktop (installed Windows, macOS or Linux apps): `platforms/desktop/` or `/llms-desktop.txt`.
- Mobile (installed iOS or Android apps): `platforms/mobile/` or `/llms-mobile.txt`.

Foundations and tokens are the same everywhere; layout, navigation, input,
component sizing and OS conventions follow the platform guide. A website opened
on a phone follows the web guide.

## Implementation rules

1. Read the relevant docs before coding.
2. Reuse existing tokens and components.
3. Do not invent new core tokens.
4. If a gap exists, propose an extension and document it.
5. Do not replace real content with decorative placeholders.
6. Report deviations and explain why they are needed.

## Output checklist

Before finishing, report:
- target platform (web, desktop or mobile);
- tokens used;
- components/patterns reused;
- responsive or adaptive behavior for that platform;
- accessibility considerations;
- deviations or proposed additions.

<!-- SOURCE: ai/context-strategy.md -->

---
title: AI context strategy
---

# AI context strategy

## Goal

Make MXNI documentation retrievable by humans, agents, IDE assistants, and language models without requiring the entire website to be copied into every prompt.

## Published resources

| Resource | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/llms.txt` | Discovery index with links to important docs |
| `/llms-full.txt` | Consolidated text context |
| `/llms-web.txt`, `/llms-desktop.txt`, `/llms-mobile.txt` | Core rules plus one complete platform guide, in one file |
| `/downloads/mxni-{web,desktop,mobile}-markdown.zip` | Platform bundle for local projects, with its own `AGENTS.md` and the official logo SVGs |
| `/markdown/...` | Individual raw Markdown files |
| `/downloads/mxni-design-system-markdown.zip` | Offline documentation bundle |
| `/ai/agent-instructions.md` | Short implementation contract |

## Recommended model workflow

1. Start with `llms.txt`.
2. Read `ai/agent-instructions.md`.
3. Identify the target platform and load its context (`/llms-<platform>.txt`) or its guide under `platforms/<platform>/`.
4. Retrieve only the relevant foundation, guideline, or component documents.
5. For large tasks, use the platform context or `llms-full.txt` as broad context, then verify details against the individual canonical Markdown pages.
6. Cite the exact page paths in implementation notes.

## Two ways to consume the documentation

**Online (fetch).** Give the agent a URL: the platform context
(`/llms-web.txt`, `/llms-desktop.txt`, `/llms-mobile.txt`) for broad work, or
a single raw page under `/markdown/` for a narrow task. Every page on the site
links to its raw Markdown.

**Local (download).** Download the platform zip, unzip it into the project
(for example `docs/mxni/`) and point the project's agent instructions to
`docs/mxni/AGENTS.md`. Links that start with `/` inside the Markdown map to
files in that folder.

## Context efficiency

Do not automatically send the full bundle to every model call. Use the index and retrieve the smallest relevant set of documents. This reduces token usage and lowers the chance of irrelevant context.

## Stability

Keep URLs stable. Avoid renaming canonical documents without redirects or an updated index. Generated AI resources must be rebuilt from the Markdown source during CI.

<!-- SOURCE: ai/mcp-rag.md -->

title: MCP and RAG integration
---

# MCP and RAG integration

## Static reference first

The initial platform is static and works without a database, API, or hosted vector store. Public raw Markdown endpoints can be fetched by compatible tools and agents.

## MCP option

A future MCP server may expose tools such as:
- `search_mxni_docs(query)`
- `get_mxni_document(path)`
- `get_mxni_tokens()`
- `get_mxni_component(name)`

The server should read from the same versioned Markdown and token sources. It must not maintain a divergent copy.

## RAG option

For larger documentation sets:
1. Split Markdown by headings and semantic sections.
2. Preserve file path, heading, version, and last-updated metadata.
3. Embed chunks and store metadata.
4. Retrieve relevant chunks for a task.
5. Include source paths in model context.
6. Re-index after each release.

## Security

Public design documentation can be indexed publicly. Never add secrets, private product roadmaps, customer data, credentials, or internal security details to public Markdown.

<!-- SOURCE: brand/identity.md -->

title: Brand identity
---

# Brand identity

## Esencia

**MXNI** es una identidad para un ecosistema de tecnología, software, ingeniería y contenido educativo.

### Propósito

Hacer que los productos y experiencias tecnológicas sean reconocibles, coherentes y claros, sin sacrificar personalidad.

### Personalidad

| Atributo | Significado visual |
|---|---|
| Technical | Precisión, estructura, claridad y detalle |
| Modular | Sistemas, bloques, grids y composición |
| Expressive | Contraste, acentos y personalidad |
| Balanced | Futurismo controlado, no ruido visual |
| Accessible | Jerarquía, legibilidad e interacción clara |

## Principios no negociables

1. La función y legibilidad tienen prioridad sobre la decoración.
2. El color de marca no debe competir con el contenido.
3. Las superficies oscuras crean el lienzo; los acentos crean jerarquía.
4. La composición debe sentirse intencional y modular.
5. Los productos pueden tener personalidad propia sin romper los fundamentos.
6. No utilizar efectos de neón como sustituto de una buena jerarquía visual.

## Tagline

**One identity. Multiple products. A consistent experience.**

## Arquitectura de marca

- **MXNI Web:** sitios, portfolio y landing pages.
- **MXNI Software:** aplicaciones, herramientas y productos SaaS.
- **MXNI Media:** contenido educativo, social y editorial.
- **MXNI Docs:** documentación, conocimiento y recursos técnicos.

Los nombres anteriores son familias de expresión, no necesariamente marcas independientes.

<!-- SOURCE: brand/logo.md -->

---
title: Logo
---

# Logo

## Firma principal

La firma es el logotipo MXNI oficial, sin elementos añadidos: no se coloca
guion bajo, cursor ni otro signo después del logo.

## Variantes

| Variante | Archivo | Uso |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Oficial** | [`/brand/mxni-logo.svg`](/brand/mxni-logo.svg) | Morado `#6C387A` y naranja `#F7941D`. Archivo maestro; es el que usa este sitio. |
| **Primary** | [`/brand/mxni-logo-white.svg`](/brand/mxni-logo-white.svg) | MXNI en blanco sobre fondo oscuro. |
| **Purple** | [`/brand/mxni-logo-purple.svg`](/brand/mxni-logo-purple.svg) | MXNI en morado sobre fondos claros o neutros. |
| **Monochrome** | [`/brand/mxni-logo-mono.svg`](/brand/mxni-logo-mono.svg) | Una sola tinta (`currentColor`) para impresión o bajo contraste de marca. |

<div class="logo-preview">
  <img src="/brand/mxni-logo.svg" alt="Logo MXNI oficial" />
</div>

El logotipo se usa siempre con sus colores originales. Las variantes de una
sola tinta quedan para casos donde el color no es posible (impresión, sellos,
fondos que lo exijan).

## Construcción

- Lienzo del logo: `2048 × 716` (proporción ≈ 2.86 : 1).
- Cuatro piezas: **M** y **X** en morado; la **V** naranja y la **I** (naranja con
  el triángulo morado superior) forman juntas la **N** de MXNI.
- Las piezas se superponen: M en `x = 0`, X en `x = 574`, V en `x = 1025`,
  I en `x = 1858`. No separarlas ni redistribuirlas.

## Reglas

- No estirar, inclinar ni rotar el logotipo.
- No alterar la relación entre letras.
- No añadir sombras o glow permanentes al archivo maestro.
- No colocar sobre fondos que comprometan contraste.
- Mantener una zona libre mínima equivalente a la altura de la letra M.
- No reconstruir el logo con una fuente distinta si existe un SVG oficial.

## Origen

Los SVG de `public/brand/` son los vectores oficiales, tomados del sprite de
moibaldenegro.com (`mxvi-m`, `mxvi-x`, `mxvi-v`, `mxvi-i`) y compuestos con
las posiciones del logotipo maestro. Si el logo cambia, actualizar primero el
sprite del sitio y regenerar estas variantes.

<!-- SOURCE: brand/visual-language.md -->

---
title: Visual language
---

# Visual language

## Dirección

Dark Tech / Modular Bento / Developer Aesthetic.

MXNI debe sentirse como una extensión visual de un entorno de ingeniería moderno: oscuro, preciso, estructurado y expresivo.

## Recursos gráficos

- Grids y líneas técnicas discretas.
- Paneles rectangulares y superficies por capas.
- Geometría abstracta y modular.
- Gradientes localizados entre morado y magenta.
- Cyan para contraste y señales interactivas.
- Lime para datos o highlights puntuales.
- Ruido y texturas con opacidad baja.

## Evitar

- Cyberpunk genérico con exceso de neón.
- Circuitos aleatorios como decoración universal.
- Rojo/naranja como colores dominantes de marca.
- Glow en todos los elementos.
- Gradientes arcoíris.
- Interfaces que parezcan HUD de videojuego sin necesidad funcional.

## Fotografía

La fotografía debe ser auténtica y conservar su jerarquía. No cubrir rostros, manos relevantes ni elementos esenciales con overlays. Corregir exposición y temperatura antes de aplicar efectos.


---

<!-- SOURCE: components/buttons.md -->

---
title: Buttons
---

# Buttons

## Purpose

Buttons trigger an action. Use links for navigation.

## Variants

| Variant | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Primary | Main action in a context |
| Secondary | Supporting action |
| Ghost | Low-emphasis action |
| Destructive | Irreversible or dangerous action |

## Rules

- Prefer one primary button per action group.
- Label actions with verbs.
- Use a visible focus state.
- Disabled buttons must remain understandable; explain unavailable actions when necessary.
- Loading state must prevent duplicate submission and communicate progress.
- Destructive actions should use explicit language and confirmation when impact is significant.

## Sizing

Suggested heights: small 32 px, medium 40 px, large 48 px. Ensure touch targets remain usable on touch devices.

## Do not

- Use a button only for decoration.
- Use color alone to distinguish destructive actions.
- Place multiple competing primary actions side by side.


---

<!-- SOURCE: components/cards-panels.md -->

---
title: Cards and panels
---

# Cards and panels

## Purpose

Cards group related information. Panels provide a larger structural region.

## Surface hierarchy

- Base: `--mxni-bg`
- Surface: `--mxni-surface`
- Elevated: `--mxni-elevated`

## Rules

- Use borders to define structure.
- Use elevation sparingly.
- Avoid nesting cards inside cards without a clear information hierarchy.
- Keep card actions predictable.
- A clickable card must have an accessible name and keyboard behavior.
- Do not make an entire card clickable if it contains multiple independent actions without careful interaction design.

## Bento cards

Bento cards may vary in span and height. Keep consistent gutters, alignment, and responsive order.


---

<!-- SOURCE: components/feedback.md -->

---
title: Feedback components
---

# Feedback components

## Toasts

Use for brief, non-blocking feedback. Do not put essential instructions only in a toast.

## Alerts

Use inline alerts for persistent or contextual messages. Include a title or clear status label.

## Dialogs

Use dialogs for focused decisions or tasks. Provide a title, clear actions, keyboard focus management, Escape behavior where appropriate, and a way to close when safe.

## Badges

Use badges for compact metadata and statuses. Pair color with text or icon; avoid using badges as decoration.

## Progress

Show progress for operations with meaningful duration. Use determinate progress only when the amount of work is known.


---

<!-- SOURCE: components/inputs.md -->

---
title: Inputs
---

# Inputs

## Supported patterns

- Text field
- Password field
- Search field
- Textarea
- Select
- Checkbox
- Radio group
- Switch

## Anatomy

A field should include a label, control, optional hint, and validation message. Placeholder text is not a replacement for a label.

## States

Default, hover, focus-visible, filled, disabled, read-only, invalid, and loading where applicable.

## Rules

- Keep labels persistent.
- Explain format requirements before or beside the field.
- Associate errors programmatically with the control.
- Preserve entered values when validation fails.
- Do not communicate validation only through a red border.
- Use native controls where they provide better accessibility and platform behavior.


---

<!-- SOURCE: components/navigation.md -->

---
title: Navigation
---

# Navigation

## Patterns

- Primary navigation: top-level destinations.
- Sidebar: section-level navigation.
- Tabs: peer views within one context.
- Breadcrumbs: location in a hierarchy.
- Pagination: sequential result sets.

## Rules

- Show the current location clearly.
- Use links for navigation and buttons for actions.
- Preserve logical keyboard order.
- Do not rely on hover-only menus.
- On mobile, provide a clear and accessible navigation disclosure.
- Keep labels concise and recognizable.

Platform patterns (URL and top bar on web, sidebars and menus on desktop,
bottom navigation and back stacks on mobile) are described in each platform
guide: [Web](/platforms/web/navigation), [Desktop](/platforms/desktop/navigation),
[Mobile](/platforms/mobile/navigation).


---

<!-- SOURCE: components/overview.md -->

---
title: Components overview
---

# Components overview

This section defines the intended contracts for reusable MXNI components. It is a design specification, not yet a published component library.

## Component principles

1. Components consume design tokens.
2. Components expose semantic states.
3. Components support keyboard interaction.
4. Components do not hardcode product-specific brand colors.
5. Variants should solve real use cases, not create arbitrary customization.
6. Composition is preferred over a large number of configuration props.

## State model

Interactive components should consider:

- Default
- Hover
- Focus-visible
- Active / pressed
- Disabled
- Loading
- Error / invalid
- Selected (when applicable)

## Naming

Use clear names such as `Button`, `TextField`, `Card`, `Badge`, `Dialog`, and `Toast`. Keep implementation-specific names out of design documentation unless they are part of the public API.

## Platform adaptation

The contracts on these pages apply to every platform. Sizes, input methods and
OS conventions are adapted in each platform guide:
[Web](/platforms/web/components), [Desktop](/platforms/desktop/components),
[Mobile](/platforms/mobile/components).

## Component maturity

Every component should be marked:
- **Proposed:** documented, not implemented.
- **Experimental:** implemented but API may change.
- **Stable:** reviewed, tested, and safe to reuse.
- **Deprecated:** replacement and removal timeline documented.


---

<!-- SOURCE: foundations/accessibility.md -->

---
title: Accessibility
---

# Accessibility

Accessibility is a product requirement, not a visual variant.

## Minimum requirements

- WCAG 2.2 AA is the target for web products.
- Semantic HTML and meaningful heading order.
- Keyboard access for all interactive controls.
- Visible focus state with sufficient contrast.
- Form controls have labels and understandable errors.
- Images have appropriate alternative text.
- Color is never the only way to communicate meaning.
- Motion-sensitive users can reduce non-essential motion.
- Touch targets should be comfortably usable; aim for at least 44 × 44 CSS px where practical.

## Dark UI considerations

Dark interfaces can cause low-contrast text and controls. Test actual combinations; do not rely on visual intuition.

## Focus

Use a clearly visible outline or ring. Do not remove the browser focus indicator without replacing it.

## Validation

Use automated checks (for example axe) and manual keyboard/screen-reader testing. Automated tools do not prove full accessibility.

title: Color

# Color

Los colores son decisiones iniciales de MXNI v1.0 y deben validarse en interfaces y contenido reales.

## Core palette

<div class="mxni-swatch-grid">
  <div class="mxni-swatch"><div class="mxni-swatch__color" style="background:#09070D"></div><div class="mxni-swatch__meta"><b>Void</b><code>#09070D</code>Background</div></div>
  <div class="mxni-swatch"><div class="mxni-swatch__color" style="background:#15111C"></div><div class="mxni-swatch__meta"><b>Surface</b><code>#15111C</code>Containers</div></div>
  <div class="mxni-swatch"><div class="mxni-swatch__color" style="background:#211A2B"></div><div class="mxni-swatch__meta"><b>Elevated</b><code>#211A2B</code>Raised surfaces</div></div>
  <div class="mxni-swatch"><div class="mxni-swatch__color" style="background:#382C42"></div><div class="mxni-swatch__meta"><b>Border</b><code>#382C42</code>Dividers</div></div>
  <div class="mxni-swatch"><div class="mxni-swatch__color" style="background:#A83FE0"></div><div class="mxni-swatch__meta"><b>Electric Purple</b><code>#A83FE0</code>Primary brand</div></div>
  <div class="mxni-swatch"><div class="mxni-swatch__color" style="background:#E044C5"></div><div class="mxni-swatch__meta"><b>Neon Magenta</b><code>#E044C5</code>Expressive accent</div></div>
  <div class="mxni-swatch"><div class="mxni-swatch__color" style="background:#24CDE0"></div><div class="mxni-swatch__meta"><b>Digital Cyan</b><code>#24CDE0</code>Interactive accent</div></div>
  <div class="mxni-swatch"><div class="mxni-swatch__color" style="background:#B5F52D"></div><div class="mxni-swatch__meta"><b>Signal Lime</b><code>#B5F52D</code>Data highlight</div></div>
</div>

## Semantic colors

Semantic colors communicate meaning, not brand identity. Initial defaults:

| Token | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Success | `#39C98A` | Successful operation |
| Warning | `#F3B64B` | Caution or pending |
| Danger | `#F05B72` | Error or destructive action |
| Info | `#24CDE0` | Neutral information |

Do not use lime as the only indicator of success or red as the only indicator of error. Include labels, icons, or text.

## Usage ratios

As a starting point for dark interfaces:

- 65–75% dark backgrounds and surfaces.
- 15–25% neutral text and structural elements.
- 5–10% brand and accent colors.

These are visual heuristics, not strict pixel quotas.

## Contrast

Check text and interactive states against their actual backgrounds. Normal text should target WCAG 2.2 AA contrast (4.5:1); large text and meaningful UI graphics should target at least 3:1 where applicable. Do not assume a brand color is accessible on every surface.

## Rules

- Purple is the primary brand signal.
- Magenta is expressive, not a default action color.
- Cyan highlights interaction and technical information.
- Lime is a limited highlight for data and status.
- Use neutral text for long reading.
- Never use all accents at equal intensity in one composition.


---

<!-- SOURCE: foundations/geometry-effects.md -->

---
title: Geometry and effects
---

# Geometry and effects

## Radius

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---:|---|
| `radius-sm` | 2 px | Tags, tight controls |
| `radius-md` | 6 px | Inputs, cards, buttons |
| `radius-lg` | 10 px | Large panels and media |
| `radius-pill` | 999 px | Pills only |

MXNI favors controlled corners over overly rounded, playful surfaces.

## Borders

Use `#382C42` for subtle structure on dark surfaces. Borders should clarify grouping without creating a visible grid around every element.

## Shadows

- Use deep black shadows for elevation.
- Use purple glow only for selected or highlighted elements.
- Avoid stacking multiple glow layers.
- Prefer a border or surface change over glow for focus and selection.

## Glow

Recommended starting effect:

```css
box-shadow: 0 0 24px rgb(168 63 224 / 20%);
```

Glow is decorative. It must not be the only indication of focus, selection, or state.

## Gradients

Use localized gradients from purple to magenta. Cyan may appear as a small terminal accent. Avoid broad rainbow gradients.


---

<!-- SOURCE: foundations/motion.md -->

---
title: Motion
---

# Motion

## Principles

Motion should explain state, hierarchy, and cause/effect. It should not delay tasks or distract from content.

## Timing

| Token | Duration | Use |
|---|---:|---|
| Fast | 120 ms | Small feedback |
| Base | 180 ms | Hover and focus transitions |
| Slow | 280 ms | Panels and menus |
| Emphasis | 400 ms | Large, intentional transitions |

Use ease-out for entering elements and ease-in for leaving elements. Avoid spring or bounce effects unless they communicate a meaningful physical interaction.

## Rules

- Provide immediate feedback for actions.
- Do not animate large areas unnecessarily.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Never use flashing or rapid strobing.
- Avoid parallax that interferes with reading.


---

<!-- SOURCE: foundations/spacing-layout.md -->

---
title: Spacing and layout
---

# Spacing and layout

## Spacing scale

| Token | Value |
|---|---:|
| `space-1` | 4 px |
| `space-2` | 8 px |
| `space-3` | 12 px |
| `space-4` | 16 px |
| `space-6` | 24 px |
| `space-8` | 32 px |
| `space-12` | 48 px |
| `space-16` | 64 px |

Use the scale consistently. A one-off value is allowed only when a layout constraint justifies it and should be documented if reused.

## Grid

- Use a 12-column grid for desktop interfaces where useful.
- Use 4 or 6 columns on tablet layouts depending on content.
- Use 4 columns or a single-column flow on narrow mobile layouts.
- Use consistent gutters and alignment.
- Bento compositions may span multiple columns but must preserve a clear reading order.

## Responsive breakpoints

Suggested defaults (adapt to content, not device labels):

| Name | Width |
|---|---:|
| Compact | < 640 px |
| Medium | 640–1023 px |
| Wide | 1024–1439 px |
| XL | >= 1440 px |

## Density

Choose density based on task:
- Marketing/editorial: spacious.
- Dashboards: balanced.
- Data-heavy tools: compact, but never cramped.

Do not make every product use the same density.


---

<!-- SOURCE: foundations/typography.md -->

---
title: Typography
---

# Typography

## Families

| Role | Family | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| Display / UI | Manrope | Headlines, navigation, labels, interface text |
| Technical | JetBrains Mono | Code, IDs, versions, metadata, technical annotations |

Load fonts locally or from a reliable font provider. For production and privacy-sensitive applications, prefer self-hosted font files with appropriate licensing.

## Type scale

| Token | Size | Weight | Typical use |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Display | 48–64 px | 700–800 | Campaigns and covers |
| H1 | 36–40 px | 700 | Page title |
| H2 | 28–32 px | 700 | Main section |
| H3 | 20–24 px | 600–700 | Card or subsection |
| Body | 14–16 px | 400–500 | Reading |
| Label | 10–12 px | 600 | Metadata |
| Code | 12–14 px | 400–500 | Code and technical values |

## Rules

- Use sentence case for normal headings.
- Use uppercase sparingly for compact technical labels.
- Keep long-form text in a comfortable line length (roughly 60–80 characters).
- Do not use monospace for paragraphs.
- Do not use ultra-light weights on dark backgrounds.
- Use line height around 1.45–1.7 for body text.
- Typography must remain legible at mobile sizes.


---

<!-- SOURCE: guidelines/bento-composition.md -->

---
title: Bento composition
---

# Bento composition

## Definition

Bento is a modular composition made from rectangular content regions with varied spans. MXNI uses it to express systems, modules, and structured information.

## Rules

- Start with a grid, not arbitrary card placement.
- Establish a clear primary block.
- Use size variation to communicate importance.
- Keep gutters consistent.
- Align edges where possible.
- Maintain a logical reading order in the DOM.
- Reflow modules on smaller screens; do not merely shrink the desktop grid.
- Avoid decorative cards that contain no information or purpose.

## Suggested grid

Desktop: 12 columns. Tablet: 6 columns. Mobile: 4 columns or single column.

## Common failure modes

- Every card has equal visual weight.
- Too many accent colors compete.
- Content is cropped to fit a shape.
- Reading order differs from visual order.
- Layout depends on fixed pixel dimensions.


---

<!-- SOURCE: guidelines/content-data.md -->

---
title: Content and data visualization
---

# Content and data visualization

## Content

- Lead with the information, not the decoration.
- Use concise headings and descriptive labels.
- Keep long-form content readable.
- Use technical labels for context, not as visual noise.
- Maintain consistent terminology across products.

## Data visualization

- Use neutral surfaces and restrained grid lines.
- Reserve accent colors for series or important values.
- Use direct labels when they improve comprehension.
- Do not use 3D effects that distort data.
- Include units, scales, and time ranges.
- Provide a text or tabular alternative when a chart is essential.
- Use color palettes that remain distinguishable for common color-vision deficiencies.

## Semantic colors

Do not use the brand palette as a substitute for a complete categorical data palette. Extend it deliberately and document the mapping.


---

<!-- SOURCE: guidelines/overview.md -->

---
title: Guidelines overview
---

# Guidelines overview

Guidelines translate foundations into repeatable decisions.

## Composition checklist

- What is the primary task or message?
- What should be noticed first?
- Which elements are structural and which are decorative?
- Is the content readable at its actual size?
- Does the layout adapt to narrow screens?
- Are brand accents used intentionally?
- Can the composition be recognized as MXNI without relying on the logo?

## Content hierarchy

1. Primary message or task.
2. Supporting explanation.
3. Context and metadata.
4. Decorative elements.

Decoration must never outrank the information it supports.


---

<!-- SOURCE: guidelines/product-expression.md -->

---
title: Product expression
---

# Product expression

MXNI supports multiple product types while retaining a shared foundation.

## Shared across all products

- Core typography.
- Core color roles.
- Spacing and geometry scale.
- Interaction and accessibility principles.
- Brand signature and visual language.

## Allowed to vary

- Information density.
- Product-specific semantic colors.
- Navigation model.
- Data visualization palette extensions.
- Photography and illustration.
- Component composition based on product tasks.

## Product families

| Family | Priority | Expression |
|---|---|---|
| Web | Brand and storytelling | Spacious, editorial, Bento |
| Software | Task completion | Functional, clear, balanced |
| Media | Attention and narrative | Expressive, high contrast |
| Docs | Retrieval and comprehension | Structured, readable, technical |

A product may add tokens, but additions must be named, justified, and documented.

## Platforms

Product families describe the purpose of a product; platforms describe where
it runs. Apply the guide for each platform the product ships on:
[Web](/platforms/web/), [Desktop](/platforms/desktop/) and
[Mobile](/platforms/mobile/).


---

<!-- SOURCE: guidelines/thumbnails.md -->

---
title: Thumbnails
---

# Thumbnails

## Purpose

An MXNI thumbnail is a finished, ready-to-upload image built from one real photograph. The photograph is the required input and stays the hero of the composition; MXNI provides the art direction around it.

## Inputs

| Input | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Photograph | Yes | — | Sharp, with the subject's face visible. Short side of at least 720 px. |
| Title | No | None | 2–4 words, up to 24 characters. Without a title, the thumbnail has no text. |
| Accent family | No | Technical | See [Accent families](#accent-families). |

If the photograph is too blurry, too small, or does not show the subject clearly, request another one instead of reconstructing it.

## Output

- Dimensions: 1280 × 720 px (16:9).
- Format: JPG or PNG, sRGB, fully opaque.
- File size: under 2 MB for broad platform compatibility.
- One finished image: no variants collage, mockup, or YouTube interface around it.

## Preserving the photograph

The person in the photograph must remain recognizably the same person.

- Do not alter facial features, face shape, skin tone, age, hair, expression, or body proportions.
- Keep relevant hands, gestures, and held objects complete and unobstructed.
- Correct exposure and color temperature before applying any effect.
- Do not cover the face or eyes with text, geometry, glow, or effects.
- Do not add people, objects, or claims that are not in the photograph or the brief.

## Composition

Measurements refer to the 1280 × 720 px canvas.

| Zone | Rule |
|---|---|
| Subject | 40–50% of the canvas width, anchored to the left or right. May bleed off the bottom and side edges. |
| Face | 35–55% of the canvas height, with the eyes in the upper third. |
| Title | The side opposite the subject, inside the safe margin. |
| Safe margin | 64 px for text and key details. Only the subject and background may bleed past it. |
| Duration badge | Keep the bottom-right 192 × 96 px free of text and faces. The platform overlays the video length there. |

Place the subject on the side that makes them look or point toward the title. Keep one focal point: the face first, the title second, and accents last.

## Background and treatment

- Darken and simplify the original background, or replace it with `#09070D` when it is distracting.
- Separate the subject with a soft rim light in the family's primary accent.
- Use one localized gradient glow behind the subject, following [Geometry and effects](/foundations/geometry-effects).
- Limit structure to a discreet technical grid or one or two rectangular modules with 2–10 px radii, near the edges.
- Keep decoration behind the subject and away from the title.

## Accent families

| Family | Primary accent | Secondary accent |
|---|---|---|
| Technical (default) | Electric Purple `#A83FE0` | Digital Cyan `#24CDE0` |
| Intelligence | Electric Purple `#A83FE0` | Neon Magenta `#E044C5` |
| Experimental | Digital Cyan `#24CDE0` | Electric Purple `#A83FE0` |

The secondary accent stays small and never matches the primary in intensity. Signal Lime `#B5F52D` may mark a single word or data point, and only when the title needs it.

## Title

- Font: Manrope, weight 800, sentence case, left-aligned, tight line height.
- Size: 104–144 px, in up to 3 lines (see [Proposed addition](#proposed-addition)).
- Color: `--mxni-text` `#F7F4FA`. Highlight at most one word with an accent color, and only if it stays legible.
- Darken the area behind the title until the text reaches at least 4.5:1 contrast.
- Use the title exactly as provided. Do not invent, translate, or add words.
- Image models can misspell text. If that happens, generate the thumbnail without a title and set it afterwards in Manrope.

## Logo

Do not generate or imitate the MXNI logo. When a logo is needed, composite the official SVG afterwards in a corner away from the duration badge, keeping clear space equal to the height of the letter M.

## Generation prompt template

Attach the photograph and paste the prompt. It works as is; edit the first two lines to add a title or change the family.

```text
TITLE: none
ACCENT FAMILY: Technical

Create a finished MXNI YouTube thumbnail from the attached photograph.

OUTPUT
One complete, fully opaque 1280x720 image (16:9). The photograph is
the hero of the composition. Do not return an overlay, a template, a
mockup, or several variants.

PRESERVE THE PERSON
Keep the person recognizably identical to the photograph: same facial
features, face shape, skin tone, age, hair, expression, and body
proportions. Keep relevant hands, gestures, and held objects complete.
Correct exposure and color temperature naturally. Nothing may cover
the face or eyes.

COMPOSITION
Crop and place the subject on the left or right, occupying 40-50% of
the width, with the face filling 35-55% of the image height and the
eyes in the upper third. The subject may bleed off the bottom and
side edges. Choose the side that makes them look toward the opposite
side. Keep the opposite side calm for the title. Keep a 64 px margin
for text and key details. Keep the bottom-right 192x96 px free of
text and faces. It must read clearly at 168x94 px.

BRAND DIRECTION
Dark, technical, modular, and precise. Darken and simplify the
original background, or replace it with near-black #09070D if it is
distracting. Separate the subject with a soft rim light in the
primary accent. Add one localized gradient glow behind the subject.
Add at most a discreet technical grid and one or two rectangular
modules near the edges, always behind the subject.

ACCENT FAMILY
Technical: primary #A83FE0 purple, small secondary #24CDE0 cyan.
Intelligence: primary #A83FE0 purple, small secondary #E044C5 magenta.
Experimental: primary #24CDE0 cyan, small secondary #A83FE0 purple.
Use only the family selected above. The secondary accent must stay
clearly weaker than the primary.

TITLE
If TITLE is "none", render no text of any kind.
Otherwise, render the TITLE exactly once, spelled exactly as given,
on the side opposite the subject: very large and heavy geometric
sans-serif in the style of Manrope ExtraBold, sentence case,
left-aligned, up to 3 lines, color #F7F4FA, on a background dark
enough for strong contrast. Add no other words.

DO NOT INCLUDE
Changes to the person's identity, additional people, invented text,
logos, watermarks, YouTube interface elements, play buttons, arrows,
emoji, rainbow gradients, generic cyberpunk styling, random circuit
patterns, video-game HUD elements, or glow on every element.
```

## Quality checklist

- [ ] The result is a finished, opaque 1280 × 720 px image under 2 MB.
- [ ] The person is recognizably the same as in the photograph.
- [ ] Face, eyes, and relevant hands are unobstructed.
- [ ] The title matches the brief exactly, or there is no text if none was given.
- [ ] Title contrast reaches at least 4.5:1.
- [ ] The bottom-right duration badge area is clear.
- [ ] Face and title remain legible at 168 × 94 px.
- [ ] Only one accent family is used, with a clear primary accent.
- [ ] There is no generated logo or unintended symbol.

## Proposed addition

The Display token (48–64 px) would shrink to about 8 px at the smallest thumbnail size, so this guideline proposes a media-specific extension:

| Token | Size | Weight | Use |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `thumbnail-title` | 104–144 px | 800 | Title on a 1280 × 720 px thumbnail |

All other values reuse existing MXNI colors, spacing, and radius tokens.

<!-- SOURCE: implementation/css-tokens.md -->

title: CSS tokens
---

# CSS tokens

The following CSS is the initial canonical token set. Copy it into a shared stylesheet or package and keep it synchronized with this document.

```css
:root {
  /* Brand */
  --mxni-primary: #A83FE0;
  --mxni-secondary: #E044C5;
  --mxni-cyan: #24CDE0;
  --mxni-lime: #B5F52D;

  /* Backgrounds */
  --mxni-bg: #09070D;
  --mxni-surface: #15111C;
  --mxni-elevated: #211A2B;

  /* Structure */
  --mxni-border: #382C42;

  /* Text */
  --mxni-text: #F7F4FA;
  --mxni-text-secondary: #B7AABD;
  --mxni-text-muted: #81768A;

  /* Semantic */
  --mxni-success: #39C98A;
  --mxni-warning: #F3B64B;
  --mxni-danger: #F05B72;
  --mxni-info: #24CDE0;

  /* Typography */
  --mxni-font-display: "Manrope", sans-serif;
  --mxni-font-mono: "JetBrains Mono", monospace;

  /* Spacing */
  --mxni-space-1: 4px;
  --mxni-space-2: 8px;
  --mxni-space-3: 12px;
  --mxni-space-4: 16px;
  --mxni-space-6: 24px;
  --mxni-space-8: 32px;
  --mxni-space-12: 48px;
  --mxni-space-16: 64px;

  /* Radius */
  --mxni-radius-sm: 2px;
  --mxni-radius-md: 6px;
  --mxni-radius-lg: 10px;
  --mxni-radius-pill: 999px;

  /* Effects */
  --mxni-glow-purple: 0 0 24px rgb(168 63 224 / 20%);
  --mxni-shadow: 0 8px 32px rgb(0 0 0 / 35%);

  /* Motion */
  --mxni-motion-fast: 120ms;
  --mxni-motion-base: 180ms;
  --mxni-motion-slow: 280ms;
}
```

## Naming

Use `--mxni-{category}-{name}`. Do not use unexplained abbreviations. Prefer semantic aliases in product themes instead of changing core tokens.


---

<!-- SOURCE: implementation/overview.md -->

---
title: Implementation overview
---

# Implementation overview

## Source of truth

This repository documents the initial design contract. A future published token package may be generated from structured token data.

## Recommended layers

1. **Design tokens:** color, typography, spacing, radius, effects, motion.
2. **Primitive components:** button, field, surface, text, icon.
3. **Composite components:** navigation, cards, dialogs, forms.
4. **Patterns:** dashboards, Bento layouts, editorial layouts.
5. **Product layer:** product-specific composition and semantic extensions.

## Technology neutrality

The visual rules are framework-agnostic. CSS variables are the baseline implementation. React examples are optional adapters, not the definition of the system.

## Adoption

A product adopts MXNI by:
- importing the core tokens;
- using documented type and spacing scales;
- mapping its components to MXNI component contracts;
- documenting product-specific extensions;
- testing accessibility and responsive behavior.


---

<!-- SOURCE: implementation/react.md -->

---
title: React integration
---

# React integration

## Recommended approach

- Import the shared CSS tokens once at the application root.
- Build accessible primitives that consume CSS variables.
- Keep product-specific variants explicit.
- Avoid copying token values into component styles.
- Use semantic HTML and native controls where possible.

## Example

```tsx
type ButtonVariant = 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'ghost' | 'destructive'

type ButtonProps = React.ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> & {
  variant?: ButtonVariant
}

export function Button({
  variant = 'primary',
  className,
  ...props
}: ButtonProps) {
  return (
    <button
      className={['mxni-button', `mxni-button--${variant}`, className]
        .filter(Boolean)
        .join(' ')}
      {...props}
    />
  )
}
```

```css
.mxni-button {
  min-height: 40px;
  padding: 0 16px;
  border: 1px solid transparent;
  border-radius: var(--mxni-radius-md);
  font: 600 14px var(--mxni-font-display);
  cursor: pointer;
  transition:
    background var(--mxni-motion-base) ease,
    border-color var(--mxni-motion-base) ease;
}

.mxni-button--primary {
  color: var(--mxni-text);
  background: var(--mxni-primary);
}

.mxni-button--secondary {
  color: var(--mxni-text);
  background: var(--mxni-elevated);
  border-color: var(--mxni-border);
}

.mxni-button:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--mxni-cyan);
  outline-offset: 3px;
}

.mxni-button:disabled {
  cursor: not-allowed;
  opacity: .55;
}
```

This is a reference implementation, not a complete production component. Add tests, loading behavior, icons, and accessibility review before publishing it as stable.


---

<!-- SOURCE: implementation/versioning.md -->

---
title: Versioning and contribution
---

# Versioning and contribution

## Versioning policy

Use semantic versioning for the design system:

- **Major:** breaking token or component contract changes.
- **Minor:** backward-compatible tokens, components, or guidelines.
- **Patch:** corrections, clarifications, and non-breaking refinements.

The documentation site and future component package should communicate the design-system version they implement.

## Change process

1. Open an issue or proposal explaining the problem.
2. Identify affected tokens, components, products, and docs.
3. Include before/after examples.
4. Check accessibility and responsive behavior.
5. Update canonical Markdown and implementation artifacts.
6. Review and merge.
7. Publish a release note.

## Deprecation

A deprecated token or component must include:
- reason for deprecation;
- replacement;
- migration example;
- earliest removal version.

## Definition of done

- Documentation updated.
- Examples verified.
- Accessibility considered.
- No duplicate token introduced.
- Build and documentation checks pass.

**Estado:** propuesta inicial v1.0. Los tokens y reglas de esta documentación son la fuente de verdad inicial de MXNI. Las decisiones aún no validadas en productos reales deben tratarse como propuestas, no como estándares inmutables.

## La idea

MXNI es un sistema visual compartido por un ecosistema de productos. No busca que todos los productos se vean idénticos: busca que todos hablen el mismo lenguaje.

**Technical. Modular. Expressive.**
